    • Find gaps in a foundation shade range

Summarise foundation shade supply by lightness band

shade_supply.Rd

Splits foundation shades into deep, medium and light bands using lightness cut-offs, then counts how many shades and how many distinct products fall in each band. Use it to see where shade supply is thin.

Usage

shade_supply(shades, breaks = c(0.45, 0.7))

Arguments

shades

A data frame with columns brand, product and lightness, such as foundation_shades.

breaks

Two increasing numbers between 0 and 1 giving the lightness cut-offs between deep and medium, and between medium and light.

Value

A data frame with one row per band (Deep, Medium, Light) and columns:

band

Lightness band

n_shades

Number of shades in the band

n_products

Number of distinct products offering at least one shade in the band

share

Proportion of all shades that fall in the band

shades_per_product

Average number of shades per product offering the band; NA when no product offers it

Bands with no shades are kept with zero counts.

Examples

shade_supply(foundation_shades)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   band   n_shades n_products share shades_per_product
#>   <fct>     <int>      <int> <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1 Deep       1083        221 0.160               4.90
#> 2 Medium     3094        310 0.457               9.98
#> 3 Light      2597        302 0.383               8.60
# Deep shades are a small share of supply, and products offering them
# tend to offer fewer deep options

shade_supply(foundation_shades, breaks = c(0.40, 0.75))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   band   n_shades n_products share shades_per_product
#>   <fct>     <int>      <int> <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1 Deep        735        188 0.109               3.91
#> 2 Medium     4226        315 0.624              13.4 
#> 3 Light      1813        286 0.268               6.34
# Check whether the conclusion holds under a different band definition
